account.$comment: Profile for auth: fresh — the harness registers this account through the app's own sign-up API (lib/account.mjs). nickname defaults to name, birthYear to this year − age.

persona.purpose: Find study partners for his classes and a cheap way to get places — he commutes from Oakland and has no car.

language.notes: Bilingual English/Spanish; uses apps in English.

persona.backstory: I transferred this fall and I'm on campus maybe four days a week between BART and work shifts. Everyone already knows each other from freshman year. I don't have time to scroll through stuff — I open an app between classes, and if it doesn't help me in a minute or two I close it. I'd love people in my classes to study with.
quitsWhen: It wastes my time between classes
I can't tell what to tap next
persona.voice: Direct and practical. 'OK, where's the…', 'I don't have time for this'.

scenario.title: Brand-new account: find someone on campus to hang out with this week
scenario.goal: You just heard about this app and want someone on campus to hang out with this week. Make an account with your school e-mail, then use the app to find a person or plan you could join this week and tell them you're in.

setup.notes: Fresh account: sample profiles are shown only to demo accounts, so a new real user sees what a real first-week student sees (cold start).

success.description: Signed up during the run AND, as that new account, joined/requested a plan, hosted one, sent a friend request or sent a chat message.

record.description: the account the browser is signed in to was created during this run
joined or asked to join a plan

environment.summary: Local stack: this worktree's server + built web app, fresh seeded FileStore per run, no secrets, no worker.
knownLimits: Dining menus and RSF gym crowd levels need live campus sources (the local stack runs with CAMPUS_LIVE=0) — empty or missing data there is not a UX bug.
AI features (Ask Lumi, AI profile draft on /start, conversation starters) need an OpenAI key; none is configured locally.

Course catalog is the built-in sample list (~210 courses, e.g. MATH 1A; no cached catalog — run `local-stack catalog fetch` once (about 5 minutes) to test with the real Berkeley schedule). Live has the imported current-term Berkeley schedule (e.g. MATH 51) — course-name findings on timetable/class screens are marked environment-limited.

Campus events, free food, internships, hackathons and scholarships are a read-only snapshot of live (1302 real items, 133 events this week, taken 2026-11-02 19:15 UTC) plus the CSV calendar. Nothing new appears during the run; Q&A and reviews are empty.
No e-mail is sent: the sign-up / sign-in code is shown on screen in the hint (live sends a real e-mail).
Real-time updates (SSE) work locally; other people never reply unless the stack was started with --autoreply.
